content:
If you've just purchased a new Mac, like the recently released Mac mini or Mac Studio, you might also be thinking about buying an external monitor.

Here are my recommendations, covering multiple product categories, price points, and other factors.

Best External Monitors for Mac

Apple Studio Display

When it comes to the best monitors on the market, you absolutely have to mention Apple's Studio Display. Although it's on the pricey side, it features Apple's signature design and comes with a 27-inch 5K display.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K Retina display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: 600 nits
  • Color support: Wide color gamut (P3), supporting 1 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: 12-megapixel Center Stage camera with Desk View support
  • True Tone technology: Automatically adjusts the display's color temperature to match ambient lighting
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 5 ports (up to 120Gb/s) and two USB-C ports (up to 10Gb/s)
  • Host charging: Up to 96W

The Studio Display comes in multiple configurations at different price points, which I'll list one by one below. If you want an iMac-like experience with your Mac, the Apple Studio Display is the best choice.

Standard glass with tilt-adjustable stand

Standard glass with tilt- and height-adjustable stand

Nano-texture glass with tilt-adjustable stand

Nano-texture glass with tilt- and height-adjustable stand

Apple Studio Display XDR

The Studio Display XDR was released earlier this year and outperforms the standard Studio Display in several specifications, including mini-LED display technology and a 120Hz refresh rate.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K Retina XDR display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch, with mini-LED backlighting and 2,304 local dimming zones
  • Brightness: Up to 1,000 nits SDR brightness, up to 2,000 nits HDR peak brightness
  • Color support: P3 and Adobe RGB wide color gamut, supporting 1 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 120Hz with Adaptive Sync
  • Host charging: Up to 140W

Of course, the price of these advantages is that it costs more than the standard Studio Display.

Samsung M9 Smart Monitor

The 32-inch Samsung M9 Smart Monitor features a 4K OLED panel, making it a very attractive option for Mac users. My colleague Justin Kahn at 9to5Toys has switched to this monitor, saying that "over the past few months, it's been a pleasure to use with my Mac mini."

  • Panel: 32-inch 4K OLED display (3840×2160 resolution) with anti-glare coating
  • Refresh rate: 165Hz
  • Ports: DisplayPort, HDMI, USB-C, 2 USB-A
  • Built-in camera: Yes, 4K
  • HDR support: Yes (HDR10/HDR10+)

Although it doesn't offer the crisp 5K or 6K resolution of other options on the list, you'll enjoy the benefits of OLED, including deeper blacks, better color reproduction, and contrast.

Buy the Samsung M9 OLED Smart Monitor:

LG UltraFine 6K

The LG UltraFine 6K represents LG's high-end evolution in the display business. It features a 32-inch panel with a resolution of 6144 x 3456 pixels and offers a generous array of ports. Here are the key specifications:

  • Display: 31.5-inch 6K Nano IPS Black display (6144×3456 resolution), 224 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: 450 nits typical; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color support: 98% DCI-P3 and 99.5% Adobe RGB, supporting 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • True Tone technology: None; supports auto brightness adjustment
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 5 ports, one DisplayPort 2.1, one HDMI 2.1, two downstream USB-C ports, and one upstream USB-C port
  • Host charging: Up to 96W via Thunderbolt
  • Contrast ratio: 2,000:1

Below is the purchase link for the LG UltraFine 6K

Asus ProArt 5K Display

My colleague Jeff Benjamin had hands-on time with this monitor, and it immediately caught my attention. The Asus ProArt (PA27JCV) 5K monitor delivers the same 5K resolution (5120×2880) in a 27-inch form factor, but at half the price of the Studio Display.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K IPS display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: 400 nits typical; VESA DisplayHDR 500 certified
  • Color support: 99% DCI-P3, 100% sRGB, and 95% Adobe RGB, supporting 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz with Adaptive-Sync
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient sensing: Ambient light and backlight sensors automatically adjust brightness and color temperature
  • Ports: One USB-C with DisplayPort Alt Mode support, one DisplayPort 1.4, one HDMI 2.1, three USB-A, one downstream USB-C, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 96W via USB-C

Check out the full review above for all the details. If you're looking for a 5K monitor for your Mac, the Asus ProArt is hard to beat.

Below is the purchase link for the Asus ProArt 5K monitor:

Asus ProArt 6K Display

If you're looking for a larger, higher-resolution option, Asus has you covered there too. The new Asus ProArt 6K monitor (PA32QCV) features a 32-inch panel with a native resolution of 6016 x 3384. Jeff called it "an incredible value" in his review.

  • Display: 31.5-inch 6K IPS display (6016×3384 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: 400 nits typical, 600 nits HDR peak; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color support: 98% DCI-P3 and 100% sRGB, supporting 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz with Adaptive-Sync (48–60Hz)
  • Camera: None
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 4 ports, one DisplayPort 1.4, one HDMI 2.1, USB-C and USB-A hub connections, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 96W via Thunderbolt 4

Perhaps the most appealing aspect of the ASUS ProArt 6K monitor is its price. It's significantly cheaper than some of the most popular 4K and 5K monitors on the market.

Below is the purchase link for the ASUS ProArt 6K monitor:

Samsung ViewFinity S8 5K (S80HF)

Samsung's ViewFinity S8 5K is another attractive option to pair with your new Mac, offering 5K resolution.

  • Brightness: 350 nits typical
  • Color support: 99% sRGB, supporting 1.07 billion colors; HDR10
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient sensing: Adaptive Picture automatically adjusts brightness based on ambient light
  • Ports: One USB-C with 90W power delivery, one HDMI 2.1, one DisplayPort 1.4, three USB-A, one downstream USB-C, Ethernet, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 90W via USB-C

Below is the purchase link for the Samsung ViewFinity S8 5K:

BenQ 27-inch 5K PD2730S Thunderbolt Monitor

This might be my current favorite option. The BenQ PD2730S 27-inch 5K monitor comes packed with Mac-friendly features, the most prominent being its sharp 5K resolution.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K IPS display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch, with Nano Matte coating
  • Brightness: 400 nits typical and peak; VESA DisplayHDR 400 certified
  • Color support: 100% sRGB, 100% Rec.709, and 98% P3, supporting 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • Ports: One upstream Thunderbolt 4, one downstream Thunderbolt 4, one upstream USB-C, one downstream USB-C, three USB-A, one HDMI 2.1, one DisplayPort 1.4, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 90W via Thunderbolt 4
  • Hotkey Puck G3: Physical external controller with customizable operations

Below is the purchase link for the BenQ PD2730S 27-inch 5K monitor:

BenQ 32-inch 4K PD3225U Thunderbolt Monitor

If you want to pair your new Mac with a 32-inch monitor but want to keep the budget under $1,000, this is one of the most attractive options. However, its biggest drawback is that you "only" get 4K resolution instead of 5K. But it offers a rich selection of ports, and the 32-inch panel comes in at under $1,000.

  • Display: 31.5-inch 4K IPS Black display (3840×2160 resolution), 140 pixels per inch
  • Color support: 98% P3, 100% sRGB, and 100% Rec.709, supporting 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient sensing: No automatic ambient light color temperature adjustment
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 3, two HDMI 2.0, one DisplayPort 1.4, one downstream USB-C, three USB-A, one USB-B, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 85W via Thunderbolt 3

Below is the purchase link for the BenQ 32-inch 4K PD3225U Thunderbolt monitor:

Dell U4025QW 40-inch Ultrawide Monitor

If you're looking to pair your Mac with an ultrawide monitor, the Dell U4025QW is one of the best options on the market. It packs 5K resolution and a 120Hz refresh rate into a 40-inch display, along with a rich selection of ports, a matte screen finish, and more.

  • Display: 39.7-inch curved 5K2K IPS Black display (5120×2160 resolution), 140 pixels per inch, 21:9 aspect ratio, 2500R curvature
  • Brightness: 450 nits typical, 600 nits HDR peak; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color support: 99% DCI-P3, 99% Display P3, 100% sRGB, and 100% Rec.709, supporting 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: Up to 120Hz with VRR support
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient sensing: Ambient light sensor automatically adjusts brightness and color temperature
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 4, HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4, three USB-C, five USB-A, 2.5Gb Ethernet, and audio output
  • Host charging: Up to 140W via Thunderbolt 4
  • Speakers: Two 9W speakers

Below is the purchase link for the Dell U4025QW 40-inch ultrawide monitor:

Samsung ViewFinity S65TC

If you want to enter the ultrawide monitor market at a more affordable price, consider the Samsung ViewFinity S65TC, currently on sale at nearly half off. Although it doesn't have all the premium features of other options, you still get a 34-inch ultrawide curved display and a rich selection of ports, including a Thunderbolt 4 port with power delivery support.

  • Display: 34-inch ultrawide curved display with Ultra-WQHD resolution (3440×1440) and 1000R curvature for an immersive viewing experience.
  • Brightness: 350 nits typical.
  • Camera: None.
  • Ports: One Thunderbolt 4 port (providing up to 90W power delivery), one HDMI 2.0, one DisplayPort 1.2, three USB-A 3.0, one RJ45 Ethernet, and one 3.5mm headphone jack.

Below is the purchase link for the Samsung ViewFinity S65TC:

Summary

These are just some of the best external monitor options to pair with your new Mac. They all offer excellent macOS integration, rich connectivity options, and unique sizes and form factors.

Have you recently bought a new Mac? Which monitor are you pairing with it? Feel free to let us know in the comments.
